method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, constructor-by-constructor replay of term and formula substitution, verification of both free-for examples and the variable-capture counterexample, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Recursive substitution in terms and formulas, the free-for condition, variable capture, vacuous substitution, and quantified-formula instances.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Substitution in a term leaves constants and nonmatching variables alone, replaces the matching variable by t, and recursively substitutes in every function argument.
samples.checks: All four term constructors, the syntactic nonidentity side condition and every displayed substitution expression are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A term t is free for x in A exactly when no free occurrence of x lies under a quantifier that binds a variable appearing in t; v8 passes the test in the existential example, while f(v1,v2) fails it under forall-v2.
samples.checks: The condition quantifies over free x-occurrences and variables of t, and both examples preserve their binder and argument positions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Formula substitution replaces every free x by t and commutes recursively with truth constants, atomic formulas, equality, connectives and quantifiers; a quantifier with variable x blocks descent into its body.
samples.checks: Both truth constants, predicate arguments, both equality terms, five connective constructors and both quantifiers retain their exact substitution outputs and side condition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Substitution is vacuous when x does not occur in A at all.
samples.checks: The no-occurrence hypothesis and unchanged-formula conclusion are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Substituting y for x in exists-y(x<y) would capture the formerly free y and yield the false exists-y(y<y), even though forall-x exists-y(x<y) is true over the natural numbers; the free-for condition prevents this.
samples.checks: Every example formula, the capture mechanism, truth contrast and final prevention condition are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A(x) signals that x may occur free; when t is free for x, A(t) abbreviates the substitution and is called an instance of forall-x A(x).
samples.checks: The convention, free-for assumption, abbreviation direction and final general instance statement are retained.

source_observations: The free-for condition prevents capture rather than requiring x actually to occur, so vacuous substitution remains allowed.
The quantifier clauses stop when the binder is x and otherwise recurse, relying on the global free-for condition to exclude capture by a different binder.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The Marathi free-for, capture and instance vocabulary remains explicitly open to specialist review in T216 and T217.
